Set it when the run behind this trigger costs money (a paid model, an outside API), so a flood of calls or events cannot run up the bill. portLiterals.code:
import re
from datetime import date

# One task per line, its due date anywhere on the line:
# 2026-10-12 (ISO), or 10/12 and 10/12/2026 (month first; no year means this year).
iso = re.compile(r"\b(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})\b")
us = re.compile(r"\b(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})(?:/(\d{2,4}))?\b")

today = date.today()
parsed = []
for number, raw in enumerate(tasks.splitlines(), start=1):
    line = raw.strip().lstrip("-*").strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    m = iso.search(line)
    if m:
        due = date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
    else:
        m = us.search(line)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError(f"line {number} has no due date (use 2026-10-12 or 10/12): {raw!r}")
        year = m.group(3)
        year = today.year if year is None else int(year) + (2000 if len(year) == 2 else 0)
        due = date(year, int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))
    name = (line[: m.start()] + line[m.end():]).strip(" ,;:-|")
    if not name:
        raise ValueError(f"line {number} has a date but no task: {raw!r}")
    parsed.append((due, number, name))

if not parsed:
    raise ValueError("the task list is empty")

parsed.sort()
return {"sorted": [f"{due.isoformat()}  {name}" for due, _, name in parsed]}

ExecPython.label: Python
ExecPython.description: Run a Python snippet. Declare the node's inputs and outputs inline: `ExecPython(x: Number) -> (result: String) { code: "..." }`. Every declared input is a Python variable of the same name; one that received nothing is `None`, so an optional input reads as `if problem is None`. A file input (Image, Audio, Video, Blob, File) arrives as a plain dict with `url` (a download link minted for this firing, never written to the journal, so do not look for it there), `filename`, `mimeType`, `sizeBytes` and `key`: read `photo['url']` and fetch it. Return a file on a file-typed output by returning that same dict. The code must return a dict keyed by output port name; a missing key emits no pulse on that port, and `return {}` emits nothing. A key set to None sends a real null on a port whose type takes it (`last: JsonDict | Null`), and emits no pulse on any other port. An exception the script raises (a request it makes failing, a `raise` of its own) fails the node with its traceback, or, with `error` wired, comes out on `error` instead. Mistakes in the program always fail the run, `error` wired or not: code that does not compile, no dict returned, a key that is not a declared output (`error` included: raise to fail on purpose), a value of the wrong type for its port.
